question: What is the normal range of arterial pH in a healthy adult?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 7.35–7.45

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Arterial pH is tightly maintained between 7.35 and 7.45 by the buffer systems, respiratory regulation of carbon dioxide and renal regulation of bicarbonate

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 6.95–7.05: A pH around 7.0 is incompatible with life for any length of time

B — 7.25–7.35: Below 7.35 is acidaemia

C — 7.45–7.55: Above 7.45 is alkalaemia

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Pearl: The pH is checked with the PaCO2 and bicarbonate together, because a normal pH with abnormal gases indicates a compensated disturbance

question: A patient has pH 7.28, PaCO2 58 mmHg and bicarbonate 25 mEq/L. Which acid-base disturbance is present?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Respiratory acidosis without metabolic compensation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A low pH with a raised PaCO2 and a normal bicarbonate indicates acute respiratory acidosis, as seen in hypoventilation before renal compensation develops

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Metabolic acidosis: Metabolic acidosis shows a low bicarbonate with a low pH

C — Metabolic alkalosis: Metabolic alkalosis shows a high bicarbonate with a high pH

D — Respiratory alkalosis: Respiratory alkalosis shows a low PaCO2 with a high pH

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Look for the cause of hypoventilation — sedation, airway obstruction, neuromuscular weakness or chest wall injury — because treating the ventilation corrects the acidosis

question: A patient with pH 7.34, PaCO2 30 mmHg and bicarbonate 16 mEq/L is diagnosed as having:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Metabolic acidosis with partial respiratory compensation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A low bicarbonate with a low PaCO2 and a near-normal but slightly acid pH shows a metabolic acidosis with respiratory compensation that is not yet complete

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Fully compensated metabolic acidosis: Full compensation returns the pH to the normal range, which has not happened here

B — Normal blood gases: The bicarbonate of 16 mEq/L is clearly abnormal

D — Respiratory alkalosis with metabolic compensation: A primary respiratory alkalosis would raise the pH, not keep it below normal

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Pearl: Use the bicarbonate to identify the primary metabolic problem and check whether the expected PaCO2 matches, so that a mixed disorder is not missed

question: Which practice is correct while collecting an arterial blood sample for gas analysis?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Use a heparinised syringe, expel air bubbles, cap it and analyse immediately or transport it in ice

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Heparin prevents clotting, and expelling air prevents equilibration with room air; if analysis is delayed, the sample is cooled to slow metabolism and avoid falsely low oxygen values

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Use a plain syringe without any anticoagulant: A plain syringe without anticoagulant lets the sample clot and clog the analyser

C — Put the sample in a hot water bath before transport: Warming the sample increases metabolic activity and lowers the measured oxygen

D — Collect the sample slowly and allow air bubbles to remain: Air bubbles cause false changes in PaO2 and PaCO2

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Record the patient's oxygen flow rate and temperature with the sample, because both affect the interpretation
option_1: Use a heparinised syringe, expel air bubbles, cap it and analyse immediately or transport it in ice
option_2: Use a plain syringe without any anticoagulant
option_3: Put the sample in a hot water bath before transport
option_4: Collect the sample slowly and allow air bubbles to remain

question: What is the purpose of performing a modified Allen test before radial artery puncture?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. To confirm collateral circulation through the ulnar artery

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Occluding both vessels and releasing the ulnar artery shows whether the hand can be perfused through the ulnar artery alone, which protects against ischaemia if the radial artery is cannulated or damaged

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — To test the clotting time: Clotting time is assessed with laboratory tests and is unrelated

B — To measure the arterial pressure: Pressure measurement is not the purpose of the test

D — To check the position of the vein: The test assesses arterial flow, not venous position

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Document the result, and avoid the site if the test is abnormal, choosing an alternative such as the femoral or brachial artery
option_3: To confirm collateral circulation through the ulnar artery
option_4: To check the position of the vein

question: A patient on assist-control ventilation is having all breaths delivered at a set rate and tidal volume, even when he triggers the ventilator. How is this mode BEST described?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Every breath, whether triggered by the patient or by the set rate, receives the set tidal volume

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In assist-control mode each breath, whether patient-triggered or machine-initiated, delivers the set tidal volume at the set rate, which provides full ventilatory support

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — The patient must breathe entirely on his own: Complete spontaneous breathing describes a spontaneous or CPAP mode

C — Only spontaneous breaths receive the set tidal volume: Partial support with different volumes for spontaneous breaths describes modes such as SIMV with pressure support

D — Every breath is delivered at the patient's own tidal volume: The volume is set, not determined by the patient

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: In assist-control the patient receives a minimum minute ventilation, but the risk of hyperventilation and breath stacking must be watched
option_1: The patient must breathe entirely on his own
option_2: Every breath, whether triggered by the patient or by the set rate, receives the set tidal volume
option_3: Only spontaneous breaths receive the set tidal volume
option_4: Every breath is delivered at the patient's own tidal volume

question: What is the main purpose of applying positive end-expiratory pressure in a ventilated patient?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. To keep the alveoli open and improve oxygenation by preventing collapse at end expiration

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Positive end-expiratory pressure recruits and stabilises alveoli, increases functional residual capacity and improves oxygenation in conditions such as ARDS

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — To lower the peak airway pressure: Positive end-expiratory pressure generally raises, not lowers, airway pressure

B — To reduce the respiratory rate: The rate is set by the clinician, though it may change with improved oxygenation

C — To increase the tidal volume delivered: The tidal volume is set separately

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Pearl: Watch for the haemodynamic effects of high end-expiratory pressure, since raised intrathoracic pressure reduces venous return and can lower the blood pressure
option_4: To keep the alveoli open and improve oxygenation by preventing collapse at end expiration

question: The initial tidal volume for lung-protective ventilation of an adult is usually set at:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 6–8 mL/kg of ideal body weight

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A tidal volume of 6 to 8 mL per kg of ideal body weight limits alveolar overdistension and ventilator-induced lung injury, especially in ARDS

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 20 mL/kg of ideal body weight: 20 mL/kg would cause severe barotrauma

B — 3–4 mL/kg of ideal body weight: 3–4 mL/kg is below the usual range and increases the risk of hypercapnia and atelectasis

D — 12–15 mL/kg of ideal body weight: 12–15 mL/kg causes volutrauma and is no longer used

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The volume is calculated from ideal, not actual, body weight, so a heavy patient is not over-ventilated

question: A patient who has been ventilated for four days is being considered for extubation. Which assessment best predicts successful weaning?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. A spontaneous breathing trial with adequate gas exchange, stable haemodynamics and a good respiratory pattern

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A trial of spontaneous breathing while assessing gas exchange, haemodynamics, respiratory rate and comfort is the most reliable way to predict weaning success

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — The patient's ability to speak: Speech is not possible with a cuffed tube in place and does not predict weaning

C — A single arterial blood gas taken on full ventilator support: A gas taken during full support reflects the ventilator, not the patient's own effort

D — A stable chest radiograph alone: Radiographic findings do not measure respiratory muscle strength or the work of breathing

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Ensure the cause of respiratory failure has improved, the secretions can be cleared, the patient is awake enough to breathe and electrolytes such as potassium and magnesium are corrected
option_2: A spontaneous breathing trial with adequate gas exchange, stable haemodynamics and a good respiratory pattern
option_3: A single arterial blood gas taken on full ventilator support

question: A ventilated patient suddenly develops a rising peak inspiratory pressure with reduced tidal volume and restlessness. Which cause should be assessed FIRST?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Airway obstruction from secretions or tube blockage

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A sudden rise in peak pressure with a fall in delivered volume indicates a problem in the airway or the patient's lungs, and secretions, tube kinking or blockage, bronchospasm, pneumothorax or worsening compliance must be assessed and relieved

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — A change in the ventilator battery: Battery status affects delivery but does not raise peak pressure

B — The position of the urinary catheter: A urinary catheter has no bearing on ventilation

D — The ambient room temperature: Room temperature is irrelevant to airway pressure

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Suction the airway, check for tube displacement or biting, and auscultate both sides for absent breath sounds suggesting pneumothorax
option_3: Airway obstruction from secretions or tube blockage

question: The low pressure alarm sounds on the ventilator of a patient who has just been repositioned. What is the most likely cause?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. A disconnection or circuit leak

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A low pressure alarm usually indicates a leak or disconnection in the breathing circuit, and it is common after repositioning or handling

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Bronchospasm: Bronchospasm raises the pressure

C — A tension pneumothorax: A tension pneumothorax raises pressure and worsens the clinical state

D — A mucus plug in the airway: Mucus plugging raises, not lowers, airway pressure

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Always check the patient first, then the circuit, then the machine, because a disconnection is harmless if corrected at once and fatal if it is missed

question: What is the normal range of central venous pressure in an adult?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 2–8 cm H2O

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Central venous pressure normally lies between 2 and 8 cm of water or roughly 0 to 8 mmHg, reflecting right ventricular filling pressure

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — −5 to −2 cm H2O: Negative values are not physiological except momentarily during deep inspiration

B — 25–30 cm H2O: 25–30 cm H2O indicates marked venous congestion

D — 15–20 cm H2O: 15–20 cm H2O suggests fluid overload or right heart failure

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Read central venous pressure in relation to the patient's clinical state, since trends and the response to fluids are more informative than a single value

question: A ventilated patient receiving a fluid bolus has a central venous pressure of 16 cm H2O with distended neck veins and bilateral crackles. What does this indicate?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Fluid overload with a risk of pulmonary oedema

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A raised filling pressure with neck vein distension and pulmonary crackles indicates that the circulation can no longer handle the volume, so the infusion is stopped and the doctor informed

🔍 Key Clues: 16 cm

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — A normal response to the bolus: This is not a normal response; it is an early sign of overload

C — An air leak in the line: An air leak affects the pressure trace rather than producing clinical signs of congestion

D — Hypovolaemia requiring further boluses: Hypovolaemia shows a low filling pressure with flat neck veins and clear lungs

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Pearl: Monitor the respiratory rate, oxygen saturation and lung sounds during fluid resuscitation, especially in patients with cardiac or renal disease
option_1: Fluid overload with a risk of pulmonary oedema

question: What is the usual target mean arterial pressure for an adult in septic shock during the initial resuscitation?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 65 mmHg

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A mean arterial pressure of at least 65 mmHg is the accepted initial target, because it maintains perfusion of vital organs while limiting the vasopressor dose

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 50 mmHg: 50 mmHg is below the autoregulatory threshold of most organs

C — 110 mmHg: 110 mmHg increases the risk of arrhythmia and myocardial strain without proven benefit

D — 90 mmHg: 90 mmHg may be required in chronic hypertension, but it is not the initial general target

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Mean arterial pressure equals diastolic pressure plus one third of the pulse pressure, so it can be estimated quickly at the bedside

question: Immediately after inserting an endotracheal tube, how should correct placement be confirmed?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Auscultate equal breath sounds over both axillae, observe chest rise and check the capnography trace

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Clinical confirmation combines equal breath sounds, symmetrical chest rise and a persistent carbon dioxide waveform, which is the most reliable bedside indicator

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Attach a ventilator and observe the tidal volume alone: Delivered volume alone does not prove tracheal placement

B — Inflate the cuff to maximum pressure and observe: An over-inflated cuff does not confirm placement and can damage the tracheal mucosa

C — Take a chest radiograph before initiating ventilation: A chest radiograph confirms depth but is not the first check and must not delay ventilation

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Pearl: Absent carbon dioxide waveform and gurgling over the epigastrium indicate oesophageal intubation, which requires immediate removal and re-intubation
option_1: Attach a ventilator and observe the tidal volume alone
option_2: Inflate the cuff to maximum pressure and observe
option_3: Take a chest radiograph before initiating ventilation
option_4: Auscultate equal breath sounds over both axillae, observe chest rise and check the capnography trace

question: What is the recommended cuff pressure for an endotracheal tube?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 20–30 cm H2O

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Cuff pressure is kept at 20 to 30 cm H2O, checked with a manometer, which seals the airway without exceeding the tracheal capillary pressure

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 50–60 cm H2O: 50–60 cm H2O exceeds mucosal perfusion pressure and causes tracheal ischaemia

C — 5–10 cm H2O: Below 20 cm H2O the seal is unreliable and secretions leak into the lungs

D — 80–100 cm H2O: Such pressure causes mucosal necrosis, stenosis and tracheo-oesophageal fistula

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Pearl: Measure the cuff pressure at least every shift, and never use the finger-feel method, which overestimates the pressure

question: Which action should precede endotracheal suctioning?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Pre-oxygenation with a higher inspired oxygen fraction and explanation to the patient

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Pre-oxygenation prevents the hypoxaemia that inevitably accompanies suctioning, and explaining the procedure reduces anxiety and helps the patient cooperate

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Rapid saline instillation into the tube: Routine saline instillation increases infection and hypoxaemia and is not recommended

C — Full neck extension to straighten the airway: Neck extension is unnecessary and can be hazardous in a patient with a cervical injury

D — Disconnection of the ventilator for two minutes: Prolonged disconnection allows atelectasis and desaturation

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Pearl: Limit each suction pass to 10 to 15 seconds, use the appropriate catheter size and monitor the heart rate and oxygen saturation throughout
option_2: Pre-oxygenation with a higher inspired oxygen fraction and explanation to the patient
option_3: Full neck extension to straighten the airway
option_4: Disconnection of the ventilator for two minutes

question: When is endotracheal suctioning indicated?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Only when the patient has visible secretions, a coarse breath sound or a rising airway pressure — not on a fixed schedule

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Suctioning is performed on clinical indication, because unnecessary suctioning damages the mucosa and causes hypoxaemia, bleeding and infection

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Once every shift regardless of findings: A fixed schedule ignores the patient's condition

C — Every hour for every ventilated patient: Hourly suctioning for all patients causes avoidable harm

D — Only when the doctor requests it: The nurse can and should initiate suctioning when indicated, and not wait for an order

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Signs that indicate suctioning include visible secretions, reduced oxygen saturation, coarse or diminished breath sounds, and a rising peak pressure or sawtooth pattern on the flow-time waveform
option_2: Only when the patient has visible secretions, a coarse breath sound or a rising airway pressure — not on a fixed schedule

question: Which measure reduces the risk of ventilator-associated pneumonia?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Keeping the head of the bed elevated to 30–45 degrees and providing regular oral care

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Head elevation reduces aspiration of gastric contents and oral care reduces the bacterial load in the oropharynx, which is the main source of organisms causing ventilator-associated pneumonia

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Changing the ventilator circuit every shift: Routine circuit changes increase infection risk and are not recommended

C — Using routine prophylactic broad-spectrum antibiotics: Prophylactic antibiotics promote resistance and are not a prevention measure

D — Keeping the patient flat and using the same suction catheter repeatedly: Lying flat promotes aspiration, and reusing an improperly cleaned catheter introduces organisms

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Include daily assessment for weaning and sedation interruption in the bundle, since fewer ventilator days means fewer infections
option_2: Keeping the head of the bed elevated to 30–45 degrees and providing regular oral care
option_4: Keeping the patient flat and using the same suction catheter repeatedly

question: The volume of air moved into or out of the lungs during a normal quiet breath is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Tidal volume

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Tidal volume is the volume of a normal quiet breath, about 6 to 8 mL/kg of ideal body weight in an adult

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Vital capacity: Vital capacity is the maximum volume exhaled after a maximum inspiration

C — Residual volume: Residual volume is the air remaining in the lungs after a maximal expiration

D — Functional residual capacity: Functional residual capacity is the volume remaining after a normal expiration

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: Ventilator tidal volume is set from ideal body weight and is checked with a spirometer, because a measured tidal volume that falls below the set value signals a leak or a change in compliance

question: Anatomical dead space refers to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. The volume of the conducting airways where gas exchange does not occur

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Approximately 150 mL of each breath fills the nose, pharynx, trachea and bronchi, where no gas exchange takes place

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — The volume of air remaining after expiration: The volume remaining after expiration is the residual volume

B — The volume of air exhaled forcefully: The forcefully exhaled volume is the expiratory reserve volume

D — The volume of air in the alveoli: Alveolar volume is the site of gas exchange and forms part of the physiological dead space only when ventilated but unperfused

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: Endotracheal intubation and tracheostomy reduce anatomical dead space, which improves alveolar ventilation for the same tidal volume
option_1: The volume of air remaining after expiration
option_3: The volume of the conducting airways where gas exchange does not occur
option_4: The volume of air in the alveoli

question: Lung compliance is BEST defined as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. The change in lung volume produced by a change in airway pressure

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Compliance is the distensibility of the lungs, expressed as the change in volume for a given change in pressure

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — The maximum volume that can be exhaled: That describes the vital capacity

B — The rate of oxygen diffusion across the alveoli: That describes diffusion and is a distinct function of the alveolar membrane

C — The resistance to airflow in the bronchi: That describes airway resistance, which is a separate property

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: Compliance falls in pneumonia, pulmonary oedema, pulmonary fibrosis and ARDS, which is why higher airway pressures are needed to deliver the same tidal volume
option_1: The maximum volume that can be exhaled
option_2: The rate of oxygen diffusion across the alveoli
option_3: The resistance to airflow in the bronchi
option_4: The change in lung volume produced by a change in airway pressure

question: Which change shifts the oxyhaemoglobin dissociation curve to the right?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Acidosis with rising carbon dioxide and fever

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Acidosis, raised carbon dioxide, fever and a high 2,3-diphosphoglycerate concentration reduce haemoglobin's affinity for oxygen, releasing more oxygen to the tissues

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Decreased concentration of 2,3-diphosphoglycerate: A low 2,3-diphosphoglycerate shifts the curve to the left

C — Alkalosis: Alkalosis shifts the curve to the left and increases the affinity for oxygen

D — Hypothermia: Hypothermia shifts the curve to the left

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: A rightward shift is protective in febrile, acidotic critically ill patients, which is why stored blood with depleted 2,3-diphosphoglycerate releases oxygen less readily
option_2: Acidosis with rising carbon dioxide and fever

question: A ventilated patient has a falling blood pressure after the end-expiratory pressure is increased. Which mechanism best explains this?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Reduced venous return because of higher intrathoracic pressure

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Positive pressure within the thorax raises right atrial pressure, impairs venous return and reduces left ventricular filling, which lowers cardiac output and blood pressure

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Reduced airway resistance: Airway resistance is unrelated to the blood pressure fall

C — Increased systemic vascular resistance: Systemic vascular resistance does not rise with end-expiratory pressure

D — Increased cardiac contractility: Contractility is not increased by positive end-expiratory pressure

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: If hypotension follows an increase in end-expiratory pressure, the doctor is informed and volume status, sedation and vasopressor needs are reassessed
option_2: Reduced venous return because of higher intrathoracic pressure

question: What is the normal resting cardiac output of a healthy adult?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. About 5 litres per minute

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Cardiac output is about 5 litres per minute in a resting adult, calculated as heart rate multiplied by stroke volume, which is roughly 70 beats per minute and 70 mL

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — About 20 litres per minute: 20 litres per minute is seen only in extreme physiological or pathological states

C — About 1 litre per minute: One litre per minute is far below the requirement for survival

D — About 10 litres per minute: 10 litres per minute occurs during intense exercise or in a hyperdynamic state

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: Cardiac output is often expressed as the cardiac index, which is the output divided by body surface area and is normally 2.5 to 4 litres per minute per square metre

question: A critically ill patient has a normal arterial oxygen saturation but a rising blood lactate. What does this suggest?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Inadequate tissue perfusion with anaerobic metabolism despite acceptable oxygenation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Oxygen saturation measured in arterial blood does not guarantee oxygen delivery to tissues, and a rising lactate with normal saturation indicates that perfusion is inadequate and anaerobic metabolism has started

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — An increase in cardiac output: A lactate rise accompanies reduced, not increased, effective perfusion

B — A laboratory error in the saturation reading: The findings are consistent with a real physiological state and are not a laboratory error

D — Complete absence of tissue hypoxia: A rising lactate is a marker of tissue hypoxia and hypoperfusion

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: Follow the lactate trend along with capillary refill, urine output and mental status, since the lactate clearance is a useful marker of resuscitation
option_2: A laboratory error in the saturation reading
option_3: Inadequate tissue perfusion with anaerobic metabolism despite acceptable oxygenation

question: A patient receiving a propofol infusion for sedation in the ICU becomes hypotensive. Which nursing action is appropriate?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Reduce the infusion only as prescribed, assess the blood pressure and volume status and inform the medical team

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Propofol causes vasodilatation and myocardial depression, so hypotension is managed by adjusting the infusion as prescribed, assessing the circulation and escalating to the team

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Increase the infusion to deepen sedation: Increasing the infusion deepens hypotension and can cause cardiac arrest

B — Give a rapid fluid bolus without informing the team: Fluids are given on the medical decision after assessment

C — Stop all monitoring to reduce stimulation: Monitoring is never stopped; the patient is sedated, not unmonitored

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Propofol infusion syndrome, with metabolic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis and arrhythmia, is a rare but serious complication of high-dose or prolonged infusion
option_2: Give a rapid fluid bolus without informing the team
option_4: Reduce the infusion only as prescribed, assess the blood pressure and volume status and inform the medical team

question: Which assessment is essential in a patient receiving a continuous opioid infusion?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Respiratory rate, depth, sedation level and pain score

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Opioids depress the respiratory centre, so breathing, sedation level and analgesia are assessed regularly and the dose titrated accordingly

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Daily weight only: Daily weight is part of overall care but does not detect opioid toxicity

C — Colour of the urine: Urine colour is unrelated to opioid effects

D — Pupillary size only: Pin-point pupils are expected and do not indicate the adequacy of analgesia

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Naloxone must be available at the bedside, and sedatives are interrupted daily where possible to assess neurological status and reduce the total dose
option_1: Respiratory rate, depth, sedation level and pain score

question: A patient on an insulin infusion has a blood glucose of 58 mg/dL. What should the nurse do FIRST?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Stop the infusion, treat the hypoglycaemia with intravenous dextrose as per protocol and recheck the glucose

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A glucose below 70 mg/dL is hypoglycaemia, so the infusion is stopped, dextrose is given as per protocol and the glucose is rechecked within 15 minutes

🔍 Key Clues: 58 mg/dL

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Withhold treatment and recheck after four hours: Delaying treatment risks permanent neurological damage

B — Increase the insulin infusion rate: Increasing insulin deepens the hypoglycaemia and can cause seizures and brain injury

D — Give the next scheduled subcutaneous insulin: Subcutaneous insulin would worsen the hypoglycaemia

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Critically ill patients receive frequent glucose monitoring because the stress response causes insulin resistance, and both hyperglycaemia and hypoglycaemia increase mortality
option_1: Withhold treatment and recheck after four hours
option_3: Stop the infusion, treat the hypoglycaemia with intravenous dextrose as per protocol and recheck the glucose

question: Which practice is correct when giving intravenous potassium chloride?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Dilute it in the prescribed fluid and give it by infusion with cardiac monitoring, never as a direct bolus

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Potassium is a high-alert drug: undiluted or rapid administration causes cardiac arrest, so it is diluted, infused at a controlled rate with monitoring and checked by two nurses

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Add it to a blood transfusion bag: Adding potassium to blood causes haemolysis, and calcium-containing fluids also interact with blood

B — Give the undiluted drug as a slow intravenous push: A direct push of potassium is lethal

D — Administer it intramuscularly if the vein is difficult: Intramuscular potassium causes tissue necrosis and is never given by this route

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Verify renal function before administration, because impaired excretion leads to hyperkalaemia
option_1: Add it to a blood transfusion bag
option_2: Give the undiluted drug as a slow intravenous push
option_3: Dilute it in the prescribed fluid and give it by infusion with cardiac monitoring, never as a direct bolus
option_4: Administer it intramuscularly if the vein is difficult

question: Why is low molecular weight heparin commonly prescribed for a critically ill immobile patient?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. To prevent deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Immobility, central lines, sepsis and mechanical ventilation all increase venous thromboembolism risk, so pharmacological prophylaxis is standard unless contraindicated

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — To reduce blood glucose: Glucose is managed with insulin, not heparin

C — To treat infection: Heparin has no antimicrobial action

D — To increase the platelet count: Heparin can cause thrombocytopenia rather than correct it

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Monitor the platelet count for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, and check for bleeding, including at puncture sites and in the urine and stool
option_1: To prevent deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism

question: Which drug is commonly used for stress ulcer prophylaxis in a ventilated ICU patient?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. A proton pump inhibitor such as pantoprazole

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Acid suppression with a proton pump inhibitor or an H2 blocker reduces the risk of stress-related mucosal bleeding in patients with risk factors such as mechanical ventilation and coagulopathy

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — A laxative: Laxatives relieve constipation and do not protect the mucosa

C — An antihistamine: An antihistamine for allergy has no role in acid suppression

D — Oral iron: Iron treats anaemia and irritates the stomach

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Prophylaxis is reviewed daily, because prolonged acid suppression is associated with pneumonia and Clostridioides difficile infection
option_2: A proton pump inhibitor such as pantoprazole

question: A patient with acute kidney injury has an antibiotic prescribed at the usual dose. What should the nurse do?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Check the prescription against the renal dosing recommendation, clarify with the prescriber and monitor levels if applicable

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Many antibiotics are cleared by the kidney, so the dose or interval must be adjusted in renal impairment, and the nurse verifies this with the prescriber and monitors drug levels where available

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Withhold all antibiotics until renal function improves: Withholding antibiotics in sepsis can be fatal; the correct action is dose adjustment, not omission

C — Double the dose to compensate for dialysis losses: Doubling the dose without an order is unsafe and outside nursing scope

D — Give the dose as written without question: Giving the standard dose risks toxic accumulation and further renal injury

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Record the creatinine clearance, urine output and any dialysis schedule, because these determine the dosing interval
option_1: Withhold all antibiotics until renal function improves
option_2: Check the prescription against the renal dosing recommendation, clarify with the prescriber and monitor levels if applicable
option_3: Double the dose to compensate for dialysis losses
option_4: Give the dose as written without question

question: Why are vasopressor infusions preferably administered through a central venous line?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Because extravasation through a peripheral line can cause tissue necrosis, and central delivery gives reliable access

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Vasoconstrictors can cause severe local ischaemia and necrosis if they leak into tissue, and a central line provides a large, reliable route for long-term infusion

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Because drugs cannot be diluted for peripheral use: Dilution is possible but does not remove the extravasation hazard

C — Because peripheral lines cannot be used with infusion pumps: Infusion pumps are used with peripheral lines routinely

D — Because central lines are cheaper than peripheral cannulae: Central lines are more expensive and carry more infection risk; the indication decides their use

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: If extravasation is suspected, stop the infusion at that site, aspirate as per protocol, apply the prescribed antidote and document the event
option_1: Because extravasation through a peripheral line can cause tissue necrosis, and central delivery gives reliable access
option_2: Because drugs cannot be diluted for peripheral use
option_3: Because peripheral lines cannot be used with infusion pumps
option_4: Because central lines are cheaper than peripheral cannulae

question: Which nursing action belongs to the evaluation step of the nursing process?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Comparing the patient's response with the expected outcome and revising the plan

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Evaluation compares the observed outcome with the goal, and the plan is continued, modified or discontinued on that basis

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Collecting the admission history: Collecting history is part of assessment

B — Administering the prescribed drug: Administration of drugs is implementation

C — Writing the nursing diagnosis: Formulating a diagnosis follows assessment and analysis

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: Evaluation makes the process cyclical, since an unmet goal generates new assessment data and a revised plan
option_4: Comparing the patient's response with the expected outcome and revising the plan

question: Which action is essential while changing a central venous catheter dressing?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Use a strict aseptic technique with a mask and sterile gloves, and clean from the insertion site outwards

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Sterile technique with cleaning from the site outwards prevents organisms from being carried into the insertion site, which is the portal for bloodstream infection

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Clean from outside towards the insertion site: Cleaning inwards moves skin flora towards the catheter entry

B — Use a single alcohol swab and reuse the old dressing: Reusing the dressing recontaminates the site

C — Leave the site moist with the antiseptic solution: Pooled solution macerates the skin and loosens the dressing, allowing contamination

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: Bloodstream infection linked to central lines is largely preventable through insertion bundles, daily assessment of line necessity and strict dressing protocols
option_1: Clean from outside towards the insertion site
option_2: Use a single alcohol swab and reuse the old dressing
option_3: Leave the site moist with the antiseptic solution
option_4: Use a strict aseptic technique with a mask and sterile gloves, and clean from the insertion site outwards

question: How frequently should mouth care be provided to a ventilated patient?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. At least every 2–4 hours as part of the ventilator care bundle

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Frequent oral care with tooth brushing and antiseptic mouthwash reduces dental plaque and the oral bacterial burden, which is a source of ventilator-associated pneumonia

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Every 12 hours: Twelve-hourly intervals allow bacterial regrowth and discomfort

B — Only when the family requests it: Mouth care is a nursing responsibility based on the patient's need

C — Once a day: Once a day is inadequate; plaque re-forms within hours

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: Oral care also keeps the tube secure, detects pressure damage to the lips and gives an opportunity to check cuff pressure and tube position
option_4: At least every 2–4 hours as part of the ventilator care bundle

question: Which complication is prevented by turning a critically ill patient every two hours?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Pressure injury and pulmonary secretion retention

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Regular repositioning relieves pressure over bony prominences and allows drainage of secretions and expansion of dependent lung segments

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Anaemia: Anaemia is corrected by treating its cause and, when needed, transfusion

B — Hyperglycaemia: Hyperglycaemia is managed with insulin

D — Constipation: Constipation is relieved by fluids, fibre, mobility and laxatives

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: Document the turn, the position and the condition of the skin, and use support surfaces for patients who cannot be repositioned freely

question: Which practice verifies the position of a nasogastric tube before feeding?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Checking the pH of the aspirate and reviewing the documented insertion length in centimetres

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Gastric aspirate with a pH of 5.5 or lower, along with confirmation that the tube has not migrated from the documented length, supports correct placement

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Placing the tube end in water to look for bubbles: Immersing the tube in water risks aspiration of water into the lung

C — Asking the patient whether it feels right: The patient's sensation is not a reliable check, particularly if the tube is misplaced

D — Auscultating a whoosh of air over the stomach: The auscultation of injected air is unreliable and is no longer recommended

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: Feeding through a misplaced tube can cause fatal pulmonary aspiration, so the position is verified before every feed and before every medication
option_1: Checking the pH of the aspirate and reviewing the documented insertion length in centimetres
option_2: Placing the tube end in water to look for bubbles
option_3: Asking the patient whether it feels right
option_4: Auscultating a whoosh of air over the stomach

question: Which statement about physical restraint in a confused critically ill patient is correct?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. It is used as a last resort, for the shortest time, with a doctor's order, frequent monitoring and documentation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Restraint is a last resort when less restrictive measures have failed, requires documentation and an order with a defined duration, and needs monitoring of circulation, breathing, skin and psychological state

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — It can continue indefinitely once applied: Restraint must be reviewed and discontinued as soon as possible

C — It needs no monitoring if the family agrees: Professional monitoring is mandatory regardless of family consent

D — It is the first choice for any agitated patient: De-escalation, family presence, pain relief and environmental measures are tried first

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: Untie the restraint regularly, exercise the limbs and re-evaluate the underlying cause of agitation, such as hypoxia, pain or drug withdrawal
option_1: It is used as a last resort, for the shortest time, with a doctor's order, frequent monitoring and documentation
option_3: It needs no monitoring if the family agrees
option_4: It is the first choice for any agitated patient

question: Which supplement is routinely given to prevent neural tube defects in pregnancy?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Folic acid

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Folic acid taken from before conception until the early weeks of pregnancy reduces the incidence of neural tube defects such as spina bifida

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Vitamin K: Vitamin K is given to the newborn to prevent haemorrhagic disease

C — Iron only: Iron is given to prevent and treat anaemia

D — Calcium only: Calcium supplementation is given for maternal bone health and blood pressure, not for neural tube defects

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: Iron and folic acid tablets are provided under the national programme, and compliance counselling is part of every antenatal visit

question: Which change in the cardiovascular system is normally seen during pregnancy?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. A 30–50% increase in cardiac output with a fall in peripheral resistance

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Pregnancy raises cardiac output by about 30 to 50% and reduces systemic vascular resistance, which is why the blood pressure tends to fall slightly in mid-pregnancy

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — A decrease in heart size: The heart enlarges slightly and shifts upwards because of the raised diaphragm

B — Bradycardia with hypertension: Heart rate rises slightly and blood pressure usually falls

D — A fall in plasma volume: Plasma volume increases by about 40 to 50%, more than the red cell mass, which produces dilutional anaemia

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: These changes explain why a pregnant woman tolerates, and also masks, blood loss differently, and why supine hypotension occurs in the later months
option_3: A 30–50% increase in cardiac output with a fall in peripheral resistance

question: Which is a probable sign of pregnancy?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Hegar's sign with softening of the cervix

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Probable signs such as Hegar's sign, Chadwick's sign, uterine enlargement and a positive pregnancy test are strongly suggestive but not proof

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Fetal heart sounds heard on auscultation: Fetal heart sounds are a positive sign that confirms pregnancy

C — Feeling fetal movements by the examiner: Fetal movements felt by the examiner are a positive sign

D — Visualisation of the fetus on ultrasound: Visualisation of the fetus is a positive sign

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: Presumptive signs such as amenorrhoea, nausea and breast tenderness are subjective; only positive signs prove the presence of a fetus
option_2: Hegar's sign with softening of the cervix

question: How long can freshly expressed breast milk be safely stored at room temperature?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Up to 4 hours

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Freshly expressed milk can be kept at room temperature for about four hours, and it should be refrigerated earlier in hot and humid conditions

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Up to 24 hours: Twenty-four hours refers to storage in the refrigerator, not at room temperature

C — Up to 3 days: Three days is not safe for room-temperature storage

D — Up to 1 week: A week is unsafe; refrigerated milk is usually used within 72 hours

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: Store milk in clean labelled containers, use the oldest milk first, and never refreeze milk that has been thawed or reheat it in a microwave

question: Which finding on the second day after a normal delivery requires immediate attention?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. A boggy uterus that rises above the umbilicus with increased bleeding

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A boggy uterus with a rising fundus and increased bleeding suggests atony and retained clots, so the bladder is emptied, the uterus is massaged and the doctor is informed

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Mild after-pains during breastfeeding: After-pains during feeding are normal

B — Slight difficulty in passing urine for the first time: Transient difficulty with the first micturition is common, though retention must be excluded

D — Lochia rubra with a fleshy odour: Lochia rubra with a fleshy odour is the expected discharge in the first days

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: Measure the fundal height and check the pad count every shift, since rising fundal height with heavy bleeding is the classic warning of post-partum haemorrhage
option_2: Slight difficulty in passing urine for the first time
option_3: A boggy uterus that rises above the umbilicus with increased bleeding

question: The crude birth rate is expressed as the number of live births per:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 1,000 mid-year population

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The crude birth rate is the number of live births in a year divided by the mid-year population and multiplied by 1,000

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 100,000 population: A larger denominator is used for some disease incidence and mortality rates

C — 100 women of reproductive age: The general fertility rate uses women of reproductive age as the denominator

D — 1,000 live births: A denominator of live births applies to ratios such as maternal and infant mortality

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Comparing birth and death rates gives the natural growth rate, which guides planning for maternal and child health services

question: Which vector-borne disease control programme includes indoor residual spraying and distribution of long-lasting insecticidal nets?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme covers malaria, dengue, chikungunya, Japanese encephalitis, kala-azar and lymphatic filariasis, using vector control and early diagnosis

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly: The elderly programme focuses on geriatric services

C — National Programme for Control of Blindness: The blindness control programme covers cataract, refractive errors and diabetic retinopathy

D — National Mental Health Programme: The mental health programme addresses mental illness and the Mental Healthcare Act

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Community nurses supervise spray operations, distribute nets and organise fever surveys and rapid diagnostic testing for malaria
option_1: National Programme for Health Care of the Elderly

question: What is the correct flow of referral in the Indian public health system?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Sub-centre or health and wellness centre to primary health centre to community health centre to district hospital to tertiary centre

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Care is organised in ascending levels so that the patient is managed at the lowest level capable of providing the needed service, and only complex cases move upward

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Tertiary centre to sub-centre to district hospital: This sequence is the reverse of the referral flow

B — District hospital to primary health centre to sub-centre: This also reverses the direction of referral

C — Sub-centre directly to a medical college for all cases: Referring every case to a medical college overloads tertiary services and delays care

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: A referral note should carry the reason for referral, the findings, treatment given and the contact details of the referring facility
option_1: Tertiary centre to sub-centre to district hospital
option_2: District hospital to primary health centre to sub-centre
option_3: Sub-centre directly to a medical college for all cases
option_4: Sub-centre or health and wellness centre to primary health centre to community health centre to district hospital to tertiary centre

question: Which principle of health education emphasises the learner's active participation?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Learning by doing with two-way communication

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Health education is most effective when the learner participates actively, asks questions and practises the skill rather than only listening

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — One-way instruction from the educator: One-way instruction produces poor retention and little behaviour change

B — Learning based on fear of disease: Fear-based education may create avoidance of care rather than healthy behaviour

C — Education delivered only through printed leaflets: Printed material supports but does not replace interaction

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Use a planned approach with an introduction, discussion, demonstration and evaluation of what was learned

question: Which is a primary role of the community health nurse?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Providing care, health education, coordination and advocacy for the community

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The community health nurse delivers care, teaches families, coordinates services and advocates for the community's health needs

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Managing the district hospital budget: Budgetary management of a district hospital is an administrative responsibility at that level

C — Prescribing controlled drugs independently: Prescribing is regulated by law and lies with registered medical practitioners

D — Performing major surgery at the sub-centre: Major surgery is performed only at hospitals with surgical facilities

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The community health nurse also collects vital statistics, conducts surveillance, supervises immunisation and links the community with referral services
option_1: Providing care, health education, coordination and advocacy for the community

question: When a newborn is startled by a sudden noise and throws out both arms with a slight tremor, this reflex is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Moro reflex

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Moro reflex is a startle response in which the arms abduct and extend and then flex, and it normally disappears by about four to six months

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Rooting reflex: The rooting reflex makes the baby turn the head towards a stimulus on the cheek

B — Stepping reflex: The stepping reflex produces walking movements when the feet touch a surface

C — Palmar grasp: The palmar grasp makes the fingers close on an object placed in the palm

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Persistence or absence of these reflexes may indicate neurological abnormality, so the findings are recorded during newborn assessment

question: As per the Holliday-Segar method, what is the daily maintenance fluid requirement for a child weighing 20 kg?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 1500 mL

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The method gives 100 mL/kg for the first 10 kg, 50 mL/kg for the next 10 kg and 20 mL/kg thereafter, so 1000 + 500 = 1500 mL per day

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 2000 mL: 2000 mL exceeds the calculated maintenance volume

C — 1800 mL: 1800 mL would apply to a heavier child

D — 1300 mL: 1300 mL underestimates the requirement

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Maintenance fluids are withheld or reduced in conditions with fluid retention, such as cardiac failure, renal failure and raised intracranial pressure

question: Which food is appropriate as the first complementary feed for a 6-month-old infant?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Mashed cooked cereal or dal with no added salt or sugar

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Soft, well-mashed home foods cooked with clean water and no added salt or sugar are appropriate, starting with one food at a time

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Fried snacks softened in tea: Fried snacks and tea provide little nutrition and displace breast milk

B — Cow's milk with sugar: Cow's milk is introduced after one year, before which breastfeeding continues along with complementary foods

D — Raw honey with water: Raw honey is contraindicated in infants under one year because of the risk of infant botulism

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Feeding frequency increases with age, and the child continues breastfeeding up to two years along with family foods
option_3: Mashed cooked cereal or dal with no added salt or sugar

question: Which is a TRUE contraindication to routine immunisation?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. A severe allergic reaction to a previous dose of the same vaccine

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An anaphylactic reaction to a component or a previous dose of a vaccine is a true contraindication and is documented

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — A family history of allergy: A family history of allergy without a reaction in the child is not a contraindication

B — A mild upper respiratory infection without fever: A mild infection without fever is not a contraindication

C — Mild fever and mild diarrhoea: Minor illness with low-grade fever is not a contraindication

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: False contraindications cause missed immunisations, so staff must be trained to distinguish true contraindications, such as anaphylaxis or severe immunodeficiency, from unimportant findings
option_2: A mild upper respiratory infection without fever
option_4: A severe allergic reaction to a previous dose of the same vaccine

question: Which is a therapeutic play method for a hospitalised preschool child?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Play with dolls, puppets or miniature medical equipment to express fears

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Play with dolls and medical toys allows the child to act out fears and understand procedures in a developmentally appropriate way

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Restraining the child during explanation of the procedure: Restraint during explanation increases fear and trauma

C — Withholding all play to maintain rest: Play aids recovery and should not be withdrawn

D — Sedating the child before procedures: Sedation is used only when clinically required and is not a play intervention

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Therapeutic play reduces anxiety and helps the child cooperate with procedures, and it should be offered before and after painful interventions
option_1: Restraining the child during explanation of the procedure
option_2: Play with dolls, puppets or miniature medical equipment to express fears

question: A patient with schizophrenia says, "The television is sending me instructions." What is the nurse's most appropriate response?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Acknowledge the fear while gently stating reality, and direct the patient to a real, neutral activity

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Gentle reality orientation with acknowledgement of the feeling reduces distress without confrontation or collusion

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Agree that the television is speaking to him: Agreeing reinforces the delusion

C — Argue at length about the impossibility of the idea: Arguing strengthens the delusion by focusing attention on it

D — Ignore the statement completely: Ignoring the statement leaves the patient alone with his fear

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Avoid reinforcing delusions, redirect the patient to reality-based activity and assess whether the belief is driving any risk of harm
option_1: Acknowledge the fear while gently stating reality, and direct the patient to a real, neutral activity
option_2: Agree that the television is speaking to him
option_3: Argue at length about the impossibility of the idea

question: Which factor most increases the risk of completed suicide?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. A previous suicide attempt with a specific plan and available means

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A previous attempt, a detailed plan and easy access to lethal means are among the strongest predictors of subsequent completed suicide

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — A stable marriage and employment: Stable relationships and employment are protective factors

C — Occasional sadness after a quarrel: Transient sadness without hopelessness or a plan is not a high-risk picture

D — Mild anxiety before an examination: Examination anxiety is common and not a suicide risk factor by itself

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: Assessment includes direct questioning about ideation, plan, means and intent, followed by measures such as observation, safety planning and removal of dangerous items
option_2: A previous suicide attempt with a specific plan and available means

question: What is the main therapeutic benefit of group therapy for psychiatric patients?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Sharing experiences with others reduces isolation and provides mutual support and feedback

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Group members realise that others share similar difficulties, learn from one another and receive feedback in a supported setting

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — It replaces all individual assessment: Individual assessment remains essential and continues alongside group work

B — It removes the need for medication: Medication decisions remain with the treating team

D — It guarantees confidentiality is not required: Confidentiality is a core principle of all group work, and members agree to it

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse sets clear group rules, protects confidentiality, encourages participation without pressure and manages dominant or disruptive behaviour
option_3: Sharing experiences with others reduces isolation and provides mutual support and feedback

question: A hospital-acquired infection is defined as one that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Develops during or after admission and was not present or incubating at the time of admission

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The key criterion is that the infection was neither present nor incubating on admission, which is why surveillance uses time-based definitions

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Occurs only after surgery: Hospital-acquired infection includes device-related, bloodstream and respiratory infections, not only surgical site infections

B — Is present on admission: An infection present on admission is a community-acquired infection

C — Is acquired only from visitors: Sources include staff, equipment, the environment and the patient's own flora, not only visitors

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: Surveillance data guide prevention bundles for central lines, catheters, ventilators and surgical wounds
option_4: Develops during or after admission and was not present or incubating at the time of admission

question: Which precautions are required for a patient with active pulmonary tuberculosis?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Airborne precautions in a negative pressure room with an N95 mask for staff

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Tuberculosis spreads by airborne droplet nuclei, so a negative pressure room and a fit-tested N95 respirator are required, along with an airborne infection isolation room

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Contact precautions with gloves only: Gloves do not protect against inhaled droplet nuclei

B — Standard precautions without a mask: Standard precautions alone are insufficient for an airborne disease

D — Droplet precautions with a surgical mask only: A surgical mask does not provide adequate protection against airborne tuberculosis

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: Keep the room door closed, limit transport of the patient, and continue precautions until the patient is on effective therapy with three negative sputum smears
option_3: Airborne precautions in a negative pressure room with an N95 mask for staff
option_4: Droplet precautions with a surgical mask only

question: An increase in the size of an organ because of an increase in the size of its cells is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Hypertrophy

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Hypertrophy is an increase in cell size, as seen in the heart in hypertension or in skeletal muscle after training

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Atrophy: Atrophy is a decrease in cell size, as in disuse

C — Hyperplasia: Hyperplasia is an increase in the number of cells, as in the prostate or breast

D — Metaplasia: Metaplasia is the replacement of one mature cell type by another

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Cardiac hypertrophy is initially compensatory but eventually decompensates into failure because the blood supply cannot keep pace with the enlarging muscle

question: Which combination of factors forms Virchow's triad for thrombus formation?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Endothelial injury, abnormal blood flow and hypercoagulability

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Virchow's triad describes the three elements that promote thrombosis: injury to the vessel wall, stasis or turbulence of flow, and a hypercoagulable state

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Anaemia, fever and dehydration: These conditions may contribute indirectly but are not the triad

C — Hypertension, obesity and diabetes: These are risk factors for atherosclerosis rather than the triad itself

D — Infection, allergy and trauma: These are broad clinical categories, not the triad

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Immobility, central lines, sepsis and malignancy all increase thrombus risk, which justifies prophylaxis in the ICU
option_1: Endothelial injury, abnormal blood flow and hypercoagulability

question: Which parameter is a sensitive indicator of recent protein-energy status?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Serial weight with a diet history and intake record

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Serial weight, weight change, diet history and documented intake identify developing malnutrition early, especially when combined with a screening tool

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Blood group: Blood group is irrelevant to nutritional status

B — Colour of the hair alone: Hair changes are late and non-specific

D — Height measurement: Height is used to calculate body mass index but does not reflect recent change

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: Critically ill patients with prolonged illness or fasting need nutrition support, and even small loss of lean body mass impairs weaning from the ventilator and wound healing
option_3: Serial weight with a diet history and intake record

question: What is the main purpose of a written job description in the nursing service?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. To define duties, responsibilities, reporting relationships and qualifications for the post

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A job description provides clarity about role expectations and the authority attached to the post, and it forms the basis for recruitment, orientation and appraisal

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — To record the attendance of staff: Attendance records are maintained separately

C — To list the patients admitted to the ward: Patient lists are clinical records, not administrative job documents

D — To fix the annual salary of all staff: Salary is decided by the pay structure and not by the job description

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: Role clarity reduces overlap and conflict between categories of staff such as staff nurse, senior nurse and nursing superintendent
option_2: To define duties, responsibilities, reporting relationships and qualifications for the post
option_3: To list the patients admitted to the ward
option_4: To fix the annual salary of all staff

question: In research, a p value of 0.03 means that:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. The probability of obtaining a result as extreme as the observed one, if the null hypothesis is true, is 3%

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The p value is the probability of the observed result, or one more extreme, given that the null hypothesis is true; 0.03 is conventionally described as statistically significant

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — The sample size was 3% of the population: The p value has no relationship to the proportion of the population sampled

B — The result is clinically unimportant: Statistical significance does not automatically indicate clinical importance

C — There is a 3% chance the hypothesis is true: The p value does not express the probability that the hypothesis is true

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: Report confidence intervals along with p values, because they indicate the size and precision of the effect
option_1: The sample size was 3% of the population
option_3: There is a 3% chance the hypothesis is true
option_4: The probability of obtaining a result as extreme as the observed one, if the null hypothesis is true, is 3%

question: Which cardiac enzyme is a sensitive and specific marker of myocardial injury?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Cardiac troponin

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Cardiac troponin I and T are specific to cardiac muscle and rise within a few hours of injury, remaining elevated for days

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Creatine kinase total: Total creatine kinase also rises after skeletal muscle injury and exercise

C — Alkaline phosphatase: Alkaline phosphatase reflects hepatobiliary and bone disorders

D — Lactate dehydrogenase: Lactate dehydrogenase is non-specific and elevated in many conditions

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Troponin may also rise in sepsis, pulmonary embolism and renal failure, so the result is interpreted with the clinical picture and the electrocardiogram

question: A child stops touching a hot object after being burnt once. This is an example of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Learning by direct experience of consequences

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Operant principles explain that behaviour followed by a painful consequence is less likely to be repeated, which is learning from the consequences of one's own actions

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Classical conditioning of an involuntary reflex only: Classical conditioning pairs a neutral stimulus with a reflex response and does not require the person's own action

B — Social learning from a model only: Social learning occurs by observing others, which is not the case here

D — Insight learning without experience: Insight learning involves sudden understanding without trial and error

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The same principle explains why demonstrating the correct technique and giving feedback is more effective than verbal instruction alone
option_1: Classical conditioning of an involuntary reflex only

question: Which action shows culturally sensitive nursing care?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Asking the patient and family about beliefs, dietary practices and preferences before planning care

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Asking about beliefs and preferences allows care to be planned around the patient's actual values, which improves adherence and trust

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Applying the nurse's own cultural practices to all patients: Imposing the nurse's own practices ignores the patient's autonomy

B — Avoiding any discussion of culture to prevent bias: Avoiding the topic leaves unrecognised barriers to care

C — Assuming that all patients from one region follow the same customs: Assuming uniformity within a group is stereotyping and is inaccurate

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Pearl: Cultural assessment is part of routine nursing assessment and covers diet, hygiene, communication, religious practice and decisions about end-of-life care
option_1: Applying the nurse's own cultural practices to all patients
option_2: Avoiding any discussion of culture to prevent bias
option_3: Assuming that all patients from one region follow the same customs
option_4: Asking the patient and family about beliefs, dietary practices and preferences before planning care

question: Which is the first step in genetic counselling for a family with a child having a chromosomal disorder?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Obtaining a detailed family history and confirming the diagnosis with appropriate testing

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Counselling begins with an accurate diagnosis, a three-generation family history and pedigree, on which the recurrence risk discussion depends

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Estimating the risk without any investigation: Recurrence risk estimated without confirmation is misleading, particularly for chromosomal disorders

B — Providing treatment for the child's complications only: Clinical management of the child is separate from, though related to, counselling

C — Advising immediate sterilisation of the parents: Reproductive decisions belong entirely to the family and are never imposed

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: Counselling is non-directive and confidential, and it explains the condition, recurrence risk, options and support available
option_2: Providing treatment for the child's complications only
option_4: Obtaining a detailed family history and confirming the diagnosis with appropriate testing

question: What is the purpose of registration of nurses with the state nursing council?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. To license qualified persons to practise and to regulate professional conduct and standards

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Registration verifies qualification and competency, authorises practice and holds registrants accountable to a code of professional conduct and ethics

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — To purchase equipment for nursing schools: Equipment purchase is a matter of institutional administration

B — To assign duty rosters in hospitals: Duty rosters are made by the nursing administration of the institution

D — To fix the salary of nurses: Salaries are fixed by employers and pay commissions

⚠️ Exam Trap: In legal and ethical questions ask WHO has the authority to act, not who is present.

💎 PNC Pearl: Practising without registration or beyond one's competence is a professional offence, and it also exposes the nurse to legal liability
option_3: To license qualified persons to practise and to regulate professional conduct and standards

question: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes untouchability?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Article 17

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and makes its practice in any form a punishable offence

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Article 19: Article 19 protects the six freedoms of citizens

B — Article 23: Article 23 prohibits human trafficking and forced labour

D — Article 15: Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Discrimination in access to health care violates both the Constitution and the professional code of ethics, and patients have the right to equal treatment

question: How many Fundamental Duties are listed in the Constitution of India?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 11

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Eleven fundamental duties are listed under Article 51A after the 86th Amendment added the duty of parents and guardians to provide education to children

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 8: Eight was the position before later amendments

B — 10: Ten was the original number of duties inserted in 1976

D — 12: Twelve exceeds the number actually listed

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Duties and rights are complementary, and professional codes similarly combine the rights of patients with the obligations of practitioners

question: Which is the largest district of Rajasthan by area?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Jaisalmer

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Jaisalmer is the largest district by area in Rajasthan and among the largest in India, covering a major part of the Thar desert

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Churu: Churu is smaller than the three desert districts mentioned

C — Barmer: Barmer is the second largest district of Rajasthan

D — Bikaner: Bikaner is the third largest by area

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Desert districts face distinct health challenges, including extreme heat, water scarcity and long travel distances to health facilities

question: National Science Day in India is observed on:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 28 February

🧠 Clinical Rationale: National Science Day is observed on 28 February to commemorate the discovery of the Raman effect by Sir C. V. Raman in 1928

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 11 May: 11 May is National Technology Day

C — 5 September: 5 September is Teachers' Day

D — 15 January: 15 January is Army Day

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Science days are used to promote health literacy, and hospital teams often run public awareness activities around such occasions
