question: The Reserve Bank of India was established in the year:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 1935

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Reserve Bank of India was established in 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and was nationalised in 1949

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 1969: 1969 was the year of the first nationalisation of commercial banks

C — 1949: 1949 was the year of nationalisation of the Reserve Bank

D — 1921: 1921 was the year of the Imperial Bank of India

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Budgetary allocations to health are part of the same fiscal system, which is why understanding basic economic institutions helps in interpreting policy

question: The Union Budget of India is presented by the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Finance Minister

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Finance Minister presents the Union Budget in Parliament on behalf of the government, after the President's approval of the presentation

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Governor of the RBI: The Governor of the Reserve Bank announces the monetary policy, not the budget

B — Speaker of the Lok Sabha: The Speaker presides over the Lok Sabha proceedings

💎 PNC Pearl: Health allocations in the budget determine the funds available for national health programmes and hospital infrastructure

question: World AIDS Day is observed on:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 1 December

🧠 Clinical Rationale: World AIDS Day is observed on 1 December to raise awareness about HIV, to support people living with the infection and to remember those who have died

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 7 April: 7 April is World Health Day

C — 12 August: 12 August is International Youth Day

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: Awareness days are used to promote testing and to reduce the stigma that prevents people from seeking treatment

question: Who founded the Indian National Congress in 1885?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. A. O. Hume

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885, with A. O. Hume playing the key role in its establishment and W. C. Bonnerjee as its first president

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Dadabhai Naoroji: Dadabhai Naoroji was an early leader who propounded the drain theory

C — Bal Gangadhar Tilak: Tilak was a prominent leader known as the father of Indian unrest

D — Surendranath Banerjee: Surendranath Banerjee was an early nationalist leader but not the founder

question: Which organ secretes insulin?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Pancreas

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Insulin is secreted by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas and lowers blood glucose

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Spleen: The spleen filters blood and mounts immune responses

B — Liver: The liver stores glycogen and releases glucose but does not secrete insulin

C — Kidney: The kidney filters blood and regulates fluid and electrolytes

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Type 1 diabetes results from destruction of beta cells, so insulin replacement becomes essential

question: Deficiency of vitamin A causes:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Night blindness

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Vitamin A is required for rhodopsin in the retina, so its deficiency impairs vision in dim light and later causes xerophthalmia and keratomalacia

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Beriberi: Beriberi is caused by thiamine deficiency

C — Rickets: Rickets is caused by vitamin D deficiency

D — Scurvy: Scurvy is caused by vitamin C deficiency

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Vitamin A supplementation is given to children under the national programme, since deficiency increases the risk of infection and blindness

question: Sound travels fastest through:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Steel

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Sound travels fastest in solids such as steel because the particles are closely packed and transmit vibrations efficiently

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Water: Water is faster than air but slower than steel

B — Air: Air is a slow medium for sound

D — Vacuum: Sound cannot travel at all through a vacuum

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: This is why a tuning fork placed on a hard surface is heard better, and why bone conduction is used in some hearing tests

question: Which is the largest cell in the human body?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Female ovum

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The female ovum is the largest cell in the human body and is just visible to the naked eye, measuring about 0.1 mm in diameter

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Muscle cell: A skeletal muscle cell is long but slender compared with the ovum

B — Nerve cell: The nerve cell is very long because of its axon but is not the largest in volume

C — Red blood cell: The red blood cell is a small biconcave disc

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The ovum carries maternal genetic material and its size allows storage of nutrients for the early embryo

question: The chemical symbol of sodium is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Na

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Sodium is represented as Na, derived from its Latin name natrium

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Sd: Sd is not a chemical symbol

B — So: So is not a chemical symbol

C — N: N represents nitrogen

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The normal serum sodium range of 135 to 145 mEq/L is a critical value in fluid and electrolyte management

question: Which gas is exhaled in the greatest amount from the human lungs?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Nitrogen

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Nitrogen forms about 79% of the air and is not used by the body, so it is exhaled in the greatest amount by volume, although the body produces carbon dioxide

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Carbon monoxide: Carbon monoxide is not normally produced in significant amounts

C — Oxygen: Oxygen is taken up by the body, so less is exhaled than inhaled

D — Carbon dioxide: Carbon dioxide is produced by metabolism and its fraction in exhaled air rises, but nitrogen still predominates by volume

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Capnography measures the exhaled carbon dioxide fraction, which is what matters clinically and is not the same as the largest volume of gas exhaled

question: Which instrument is used to measure blood pressure?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Sphygmomanometer

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A sphygmomanometer measures arterial blood pressure and is used with a stethoscope for auscultatory readings

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Spirometer: The spirometer measures lung volumes and capacities

C — Glucometer: The glucometer measures blood glucose

D — Stethoscope: The stethoscope auscultates sounds but does not measure pressure

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The cuff width must match the arm circumference, since a narrow cuff falsely raises the reading and a wide cuff falsely lowers it

question: What is the normal haemoglobin level in an adult male?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 13–17 g/dL

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Normal haemoglobin in an adult male is about 13 to 17 g/dL, and in an adult female about 12 to 15 g/dL

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 6–8 g/dL: 6–8 g/dL is severe anaemia requiring urgent assessment

B — 18–20 g/dL: 18–20 g/dL suggests polycythaemia

C — 8–10 g/dL: 8–10 g/dL indicates moderate anaemia

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Anaemia reduces oxygen-carrying capacity and is common in women and children in India, so haemoglobin estimation is part of routine antenatal and child care

question: The fraction 3/5 expressed as a percentage is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 60%

🧠 Method: 3/5 × 100 = 60%

⚡ Fast Approach: Break the percentage into easy parts (10 percent, 5 percent, 1 percent) and add them.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 65%: 65% equals 13/20

C — 55%: 55% equals 11/20

D — 50%: 50% equals 1/2

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Converting fractions quickly helps in interpreting fluid balance and nutrition data expressed in fractional form

question: What is the least common multiple of 8 and 12?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 24

🧠 Method: 8 = 2³ and 12 = 2² × 3, so LCM = 2³ × 3 = 24

⚡ Fast Approach: Write down what is given and what is asked before calculating.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 32: 32 is a multiple of 8 but not of 12

B — 48: 48 is a common multiple but not the least one

C — 16: 16 is a multiple of 8 but not of 12

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Scheduling problems, such as drugs due at different intervals, are solved with the same least-common-multiple reasoning

question: What is the average of 12, 18 and 24?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 18

🧠 Method: Sum = 12 + 18 + 24 = 54, and 54/3 = 18

⚡ Fast Approach: Total = average x number of items. Find the total first, then subtract the known values.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 20: 20 would need a sum of 60

B — 16: 16 would need a sum of 48

D — 17: 17 would need a sum of 51

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Averages are used in nursing audits, such as the average length of stay or the average number of patients per nurse per shift

question: At what rate of simple interest will a sum of money double itself in 8 years?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 12.5%

🧠 Method: Doubling means the interest equals the principal, so 100 = P × R × 8/100, giving R = 12.5% per annum

⚡ Fast Approach: SI = P x R x T / 100. Keep T in years - convert months to a fraction.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 20%: 20% would double it in 5 years

B — 10%: 10% would double the sum in 10 years

C — 15%: 15% would double it in about 6.7 years

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Understanding growth rates helps interpret budget and workload projections in health services planning

question: ₹420 is divided in the ratio 5 : 7. What are the two parts?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. ₹175 and ₹245

🧠 Method: Total parts = 12, so one part = ₹35, giving ₹175 and ₹245

⚡ Fast Approach: Add the parts to get the total number of parts, then find the value of one part.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — ₹180 and ₹240: ₹180 and ₹240 are in the ratio 3 : 4

C — ₹150 and ₹270: ₹150 and ₹270 are in the ratio 5 : 9

D — ₹160 and ₹260: ₹160 and ₹260 are in the ratio 8 : 13

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The same ratio method is used to allocate staff or resources proportionally between wards

question: 240 is 20% more than what number?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 200

🧠 Method: If the number is x, then 1.2x = 240, so x = 200

⚡ Fast Approach: Break the percentage into easy parts (10 percent, 5 percent, 1 percent) and add them.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 288: 288 is 20% more than 240, which reverses the question

C — 192: 192 × 1.2 = 230.4

D — 180: 180 × 1.2 = 216

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: This kind of reverse calculation is common in reporting, such as finding the previous month's figure from a percentage increase

question: A can do a task in 6 days and B in 12 days. If they work together for 2 days, what fraction of the task is completed?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 1/2

🧠 Method: Combined one-day work = 1/6 + 1/12 = 1/4, so in two days they complete 2 × 1/4 = 1/2 of the task

⚡ Fast Approach: Combine rates as 1/A + 1/B, then invert to get the number of days.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 1/3: 1/3 would be the work done in one and a third days

C — 2/3: 2/3 would need four days at this rate

D — 1/4: 1/4 is one day's work, not two

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Fractional work problems mirror realistic scheduling, such as estimating how much of a task two staff can complete by the end of a shift

question: Find the next term: 2, 4, 8, 16, ?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 32

🧠 Method: Each term doubles, so 16 × 2 = 32

⚡ Fast Approach: Check the differences first, then squares, cubes or multiplication.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 24: 24 would increase by 8

B — 30: 30 does not fit the doubling pattern

C — 36: 36 would increase by 20

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Doubling series appear frequently, so recognise the ratio pattern quickly rather than testing differences

question: Which number is the odd one out: 8, 27, 64, 100?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 100

🧠 Method: 8, 27 and 64 are perfect cubes of 2, 3 and 4, whereas 100 is a perfect square of 10 but not a cube

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 64: 64 is 4³

C — 8: 8 is 2³

D — 27: 27 is 3³

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Check cubes and squares systematically when the numbers look familiar, since these are the commonest patterns used in odd-one-out questions

question: If CAT is coded as ZSB, how is DOG coded?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. CNF

🧠 Method: Each letter is moved one step backward in the alphabet: C→B, A→Z and T→S, so D→C, O→N and G→F, giving CNF

⚡ Fast Approach: Compare the first and last letters of the given pair to find the shift.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — CNG: The last letter is not shifted

B — EPH: The letters are moved forward instead of backward

C — BNF: The first letter is shifted by two steps instead of one

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Write the alphabet with positions first, and remember the wrap-around from A to Z when shifting backward

question: How is the sister of my brother's wife related to me?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Sister-in-law

🧠 Method: My brother's wife is my sister-in-law, and her sister is also referred to as my sister-in-law in common usage, though there is no blood relation

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the family tree and mark the given relations before answering.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Aunt: An aunt is my parents' sister

B — Sister: A sister would share my parents

C — Cousin: A cousin is the child of my uncle or aunt

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Questions using "in-law" relations are answered by tracking whether the link is by blood or by marriage, as only the latter creates in-law relationships

question: A person facing east turns to the right. Which direction is he facing now?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. South

🧠 Method: Facing east, a right turn moves clockwise to south

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw a small diagram - each turn changes the direction by a fixed angle.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — East: East is the original direction

B — West: West would require a 180-degree turn

D — North: North would require a left turn from east

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: Draw the compass directions and rotate the arrow step by step, which removes the risk of confusing left and right turns

question: In a row of 25 students, what is the position of the middle student from either end?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 13th

🧠 Method: For an odd number of items, the middle position is (25 + 1)/2 = 13th from either end

⚡ Fast Approach: Positions add up to one more than the total number in the row.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 15th: 15th is the middle for 29 students

C — 12th: 12th is not the middle position

D — 14th: 14th would be the middle if there were 27 students

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: With an even number of items there is no single middle position, so check whether the total is odd or even before answering

question: Some patients are diabetic. All diabetic patients need diet advice. Which conclusion definitely follows?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Some patients need diet advice

🧠 Method: Those patients who are diabetic must need diet advice, so at least some patients need diet advice

⚡ Fast Approach: Substitute into the standard formula and keep the units consistent.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — All who need diet advice are diabetic: This is the converse and is not valid, since non-diabetic patients may also need diet advice

B — All patients need diet advice: Only some patients are diabetic, so the conclusion cannot cover all patients

D — No patient needs diet advice: This contradicts the premises

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Draw the two groups as circles and confirm the conclusion holds for every possible arrangement before choosing it
option_1: All who need diet advice are diabetic
